translations.text: The Book of Ruth.

In the days of the judges, there was a famine in the land. A man went from Bethlehem in Judah to live in the land of Moab, together with his wife and his sons, because the famine had become severe in the land.
The man's name was Elimelech, and his wife's name was Naomi. His sons' names were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the land of Moab to live there.
Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
They married Moabite women. One was named Orpah, and the other was named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
Both her sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died, and the woman was bereaved of her husband and both her sons.
She and the two returned from the land of Moab, because they had heard in the land of Moab that the Lord had attended to his people by giving them food.
She left the land where they had been living, with her two daughters-in-law accompanying her, to return and go to the land of Judah.
Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, "Go back to your own country and to your families' homes. May the Lord show you kindness, as you have shown kindness to me and to both my sons who died.
May the Lord grant you mercy, and may you find rest in your fathers' homes." She kissed them, and they raised their voices and wept.
They said to her, "No! We will go with you to your land and your people."
Naomi said to them, "Go back, my daughters. Why should you go with me? Could I still have sons and give you to them in marriage?
Go back, my daughters, for I am too old to marry. Even if I said that I still had hope, and married and bore sons,

would you wait for them until they grew up, and hold back from marrying? No, my daughters. I am deeply grieved for you, and my bitterness is greater than yours, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me."
They raised their voices again and wept. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, turned back, and went away, but Ruth stayed with her.
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her family’s home. You too should return after your sister-in-law.”
Ruth said to her, "Far be it from me to turn back from you and abandon you! Wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you live, I will live. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Where you die, I too will die and be buried. May God do so to me, and more besides, if anything but death alone separates me from you."
When Naomi saw that she was firmly determined to go with her, she stopped telling her to leave.
They came together to Bethlehem in Judah. When they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town rejoiced over them, and people said, "Is this Naomi?"
She said to them, "Do not call me Naomi, but call me Bitter in Spirit, because God Almighty has made me very bitter. For I went away from here full,
but the Lord has brought me back empty. Why, then, do you now call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me, and the one who holds power in his hands has brought harm upon me?"

Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, was with her. Ruth had willingly chosen to return with her wholeheartedly. They came from the land of Moab at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Naomi had a male relative from the family of her husband Abimelech, a well-known man whose name was Boaz.

Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi her mother-in-law, "Let me go to the field and gather the grain left behind by the workers of someone in whose eyes I find favor." Her mother-in-law said to her, "Go, my daughter."
Ruth went to gather the grain left behind by the reapers, and she happened upon the part of the field belonging to Boaz, a member of Abimelech's family.
Just then Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “Peace be with you.” They said to him, “May the LORD bless you.”
Boaz said to the young man in charge of the workers, “What can you tell me about this young woman?”
The young man answered him, “She is a Moabite woman, the one who came with Naomi from the land of Moab.
She said, ‘Let me gather the leftover grain behind the reapers.’ She has been gleaning from morning until the rest periods.”
Boaz said to Ruth, “My daughter, have you not heard the proverb, ‘Do not glean in a field that is not yours’? So stay and lodge here with my young women.
Watch where they are reaping and follow them. I have instructed the young men that no one is to harass you. If you become thirsty, go and drink from the vessels the young men fill.”
She fell facedown on the ground and bowed before him, saying, “Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, a foreigner?”

Boaz said to her, “I have been fully told what you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died: how you left your father, your mother, and your family, and came to a people you had never known before.”
“May the Lord, the God of Israel, repay you and give you your reward, since you have come to take refuge under his wings.”
She said to him, “I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant. I will be like one of your servant women.”

At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come here and eat bread with me.” He seated her beside the reapers and gave her roasted grain meal. “Dip the bread in vinegar.” He set out portions of roasted grain and gave them to her. She ate, was satisfied, and had some left over.
She got up to glean, and Boaz instructed his servants, saying, “Let her glean among the sheaves, and do not harass her.”
They let her glean among the sheaves.
They did not harass her. She gleaned in the field until evening and beat out what she had gathered. She found that it amounted to about a full measure of barley.
She picked it up and went into the town. She showed her mother-in-law the grain she had gleaned and gave her some of the food she had left over after eating.

Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where were you gleaning today? Blessed be the place where you were, and the man in whose eyes you found favor.” She told her mother-in-law where she had been, saying, “The name of the man in whose field I gleaned today is Boaz.”

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “Blessed is the LORD, who has not withdrawn his kindness from the living or the dead.” Naomi also said to her, “The man is our relative, one of those responsible for redeeming our family.”
Ruth said to her mother-in-law, “He also told me, ‘Stay close to my servants until the entire harvest is finished.’”
Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good for you, my daughter, that you have stayed close to his young women, so that no one will harass you in a field you do not know.
Instead, you stayed close to Boaz’s servant women to glean until the barley and wheat harvest was finished.” Ruth lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a place of rest for you, so that things may go well for you?
Now Boaz is of our [?], the very man whose young women you were with. Tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floors.
So bathe, anoint yourself, put on your fine clothes, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not let him see you until he has eaten and drunk.
When he lies down, take note of the place where he lies. Then go over and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.”
She said to her, “I will do everything you have told me.”
She went down to the threshing floors and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.

When Boaz had eaten and drunk and was in good spirits, he came and lay down at the side of the threshing floor. While he was sleeping soundly on the threshing floor, she came secretly, uncovered the edge of his cloak, and lay down at his feet.
In the middle of the night, the man stirred from his sleep and was startled to see a woman lying at his feet.
He said to her, “What is your situation?” She said to him, “I am Ruth, your servant. But cover your servant with the edge of your cloak, because you are the one entitled to redeem the inheritance.”
Boaz said to her, “May God bless you, my daughter. You have shown even greater kindness now than before, because you have not gone after young men, whether rich or poor.”
“Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you everything you ask of me, for the whole clan of our people knows that you are a woman of strength.”
“Now, I am indeed a relative with the right of redemption. However, there is another relative with the right of redemption who is more closely related than I am.”

“Now stay here today, and spend the night until dawn. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him do so. But if he is unwilling to redeem you, as surely as the Lord lives, if he does not redeem you, I will redeem you myself.” And he said to her, “Lie down until morning.”

She lay at his feet until dawn. She rose in the morning while it was still dark, before anyone could recognize another person. She said to him, “Let no one know that I came down to you at the threshing floor.”
Boaz said to her, “Spread out your cloak.” She spread it out, and he measured out six measures of barley for her and lifted it onto her. She took it and came to the town.
She went in to her mother-in-law. Her mother-in-law said to her, “Who are you, my daughter?” She said to her, “I am Ruth.” And she told her everything Boaz had done for her.
She also told her that he had given her six measures of barley and had said to her, “Do not go to your mother-in-law empty-handed.”
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Sit here, my daughter, until you see. For the man will not rest until he presents the case today.”

Boaz went up and sat at the town gate. Just then, the relative with the right of redemption whom Boaz had spoken about was passing by. He said to him, “Come, sit here.” The man said to him, “Who is it?” and sat beside him.
He chose ten men from the elders of the town and seated them beside him.
He said to the relative with the right of redemption, “Naomi has sold me the portion of the field belonging to our brother Elimelech.”

“I decided to disclose this and let you know, and to tell you: Buy it in the presence of these people sitting here. I am the one who has presented myself to speak and to buy in the presence of these elders of my people who are sitting here. Now, if you will redeem it, redeem it. If you will not redeem it, tell me, so that I may know that you are not acting as the redeemer, and I will redeem it.” He said, “I will redeem it.”
Boaz said, “On the day you buy the field from Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the man who died, make the purchase so that you may preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance.”
The redeemer said, “I cannot redeem it, lest I ruin my inheritance. You redeem it, because of the shortcomings of my own faithfulness, since I cannot redeem it.”

Formerly, among the Israelites, this was the practice concerning redemption and the transfer of redemption rights: to confirm it, a man would take off his sandal and give it to the other man. This served as testimony in Israel.
The relative with the right of redemption said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.” And he took the sandal off his feet.
Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have acquired from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Mahlon and Chilion.”

“And you, Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, I have taken as my wife, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance, so that the dead man’s name will not be forgotten and his memory will not be forgotten among his brothers and his clan. You are witnesses today.”

The elders and all the people at the village gate answered, “We are witnesses.” They blessed him and said to him, “May the Lord make this woman before you like Rachel and Leah, both of whom built a household for Israel. Do mighty deeds in Ephrathah, and call its name Bethlehem.”
“May your household be like the household of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, and may the Lord give you offspring by this woman.”
Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He slept with her, and the Lord granted it to him: she conceived and gave birth to a son.
The women said to Naomi, “Blessed is the Lord, who has not taken away the redeemer today. You will proclaim his name in Israel.”
“He will comfort your soul and sustain your city, because your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has given birth to him—she who is better in your eyes than seven sons.”
Naomi took the child, laid him in her lap, and became his caregiver.
Her neighbor said, “A son has been born to Naomi.” They named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
These are the descendants of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron.
Hezron was the father of Ram. Ram was the father of Amminadab.
Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz. Boaz was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jesse. Jesse was the father of King David. The book of Ruth is finished.
